Marissa —

Thanks for the detail. Finance constraints / guidance:

- Minimum committed spend for a Dedicated capacity procurement this quarter is $150k ARR equivalent (we can structure monthly amortization).
- Approval lead time for new multi-month reserved capacity (vendor PO + provisioning) is currently 6–8 weeks from approval to live in our private/dedicated pool.
- We can fast-track a single-customer pilot only if legal signs off on a limited-time SOW and finance accepts a short-term credit hold; that requires an exec review and a 3-person sign-off (Sales Dir, Head of Finance, CFO) which we can try to get by May 18 if all docs are ready.

Implication: BrightLabs pilot at 4 GPUs should be structured as a time-boxed reserved instance (30–60 days) with explicit rollback if it doesn't convert; otherwise committing to full reserved capacity may breach our procurement cadence.

Folks —

Inventory snapshot (attached gpu_inventory_snapshot_0508.csv):
- US-west: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs available now (mixed 80GB and 40GB racks).
- US-east: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs free.
- EU: constrained, 4 GPUs available; shipping lead times longer.

If we want to reserve a 4 GPU cluster for BrightLabs in July, procurement needs a green light by May 22 to hit the provisioning SLA (assuming vendor lead times hold). If Finance wants a 30–60 day pilot, we can provision from pool but we need to hold capacity (remove from burstable pool) and update autoscaler rules.

Short-term mitigations I recommend:
1) Offer BrightLabs a quantized 8-bit instance profile (same model weights, lower perf) on shared hardware for the pilot start while we finalize a dedicated rack. This preserves conversion momentum.
2) If the customer insists on physical isolation, we can reassign 4 GPUs from US-west pool but that reduces burst headroom for other enterprise pilots.
3) Add a fallback policy in the SLA: if Reserved capacity is delayed >2 weeks, auto-failover to a compatible quantized variant in the same region.

I’ll update the infra Jira (INFRA-2342) with the provisioning ETA matrix and flag the racks we can spare.

—Karthik
